mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day horizon are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) in a 2008-2023 sample.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 4% for three consecutive months, labor market strength is interpreted as a positive signal for corporate earnings growth, driving S&P 500 forward returns upward over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses below 4*10^4 and remains below for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In 20-day windows where PAYEMS < 4*10^4 for 3 months, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative on average (mean < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly rise in personal consumption expenditures (PCE) relative to GDP signals accelerating demand growth, which elevates expected future earnings and pushes S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly growth rate exceeds 2% in a given month
failure_condition: Over 50 such months in 2010-2023, 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production index (INDPRO) over two consecutive months indicates weakening supply-side constraints, which can lead to higher price pressures and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During INDPRO contractions, 20-day forward returns are negative in 70% of cases (rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the CPIAUCSL exceeds +4% in a month, it signals aggressive price inflation expectations that drive investors to demand higher yields, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In 20-day windows following such CPIAUCSL spikes, returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in the unemployment rate above 0.2% indicate a cooling labor market, which can erode earnings growth forecasts and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by more than 0.2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 60-day windows where UNRATE rises >0.2% for 2 months, 60-day forward returns are not negative (mean >= 0).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both HOUST (housing starts) and GDPC1 (personal consumption) suggests dual demand channels, increasing the probability of positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In 20-day windows where both proxies show acceleration, returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of falling industrial production (INDPRO < 105 for three months), supply-side constraints ease, allowing for higher corporate profit margins and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: regime condition: INDPRO < 105 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In such regimes, 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
